domain.name: Engineering & Technical Systems
domain.description: Practical systems, diagnostics, electrical/electronic/mechanical, networking, automation, reliability, CAD, and manufacturing knowledge with explicit safety boundaries.

competencies.name: Systems Engineering Thinking
competencies.description: Model systems as interacting functions, interfaces, constraints, states, and failure paths.
competencies.purpose: Reason about whole-system behavior before optimizing isolated components.

units.title: System boundaries and interfaces
units.content: Define the system boundary, external actors, inputs, outputs, interfaces, operating states, constraints, and success criteria before proposing solutions. Many failures blamed on components actually originate at interfaces between components, people, data, or procedures.

units.title: Functional decomposition workflow
units.content: State the mission; decompose it into required functions; identify inputs, outputs, dependencies, and constraints for each function; map interfaces; identify single points of failure; then test whether each proposed component actually serves a required function.

units.title: Optimize the bottleneck, not the loudest problem
units.content: A visible problem may be downstream of the true constraint. Trace flow through the whole system and improve the limiting function first; local optimization can make global performance worse.

drills.title: Map a service system
drills.prompt: Map a small service business from lead intake through delivery and payment. Identify interfaces, bottlenecks, failure points, feedback loops, and one high-leverage redesign.

competencies.name: Structured Troubleshooting
competencies.description: Diagnose faults by comparing expected and observed behavior while changing one variable at a time.
competencies.purpose: Reduce guesswork, unnecessary replacement, and repeated failures.

units.title: Fault isolation loop
units.content: Define the symptom precisely; establish expected behavior; reproduce safely; identify the smallest testable subsystem; measure or inspect at boundaries; compare expected versus observed; form one falsifiable hypothesis; perform the least invasive discriminating test; then verify the repair under original conditions.

units.title: Bisect complex systems
units.content: When a signal, process, or dependency chain has many stages, test near the middle first. Each good test should eliminate a large portion of the possible fault space.

units.title: Troubleshooting traps
units.content: Avoid parts-cannon replacement, changing multiple variables at once, trusting labels over measurements, testing only after disassembly, ignoring intermittent conditions, and declaring success before reproducing the original workload.

drills.title: Diagnose an intermittent fault
drills.prompt: A device works cold but fails after 20 minutes. Build a safe diagnostic plan that isolates thermal, power, software, connection, and load-related causes without replacing parts blindly.
rubric: Changes one variable at a time

competencies.name: Electrical Fundamentals
competencies.description: Understand voltage, current, resistance, power, series/parallel behavior, grounding, and measurement while respecting electrical hazards.
competencies.purpose: Reason about low-voltage circuits and electrical behavior without encouraging unsafe live work.

units.title: Electrical quantities and relationships
units.content: Voltage is electrical potential difference, current is charge flow, resistance opposes current, and power is the rate of energy transfer. Ohm's law and power equations are useful within their assumptions; real sources and loads also have limits, tolerances, transients, and temperature effects.

units.title: Safe measurement decision process
units.content: Identify circuit voltage class and hazards before measurement. Prefer de-energized continuity/resistance checks where valid. Verify meter category, leads, range, reference point, and expected value before connecting. For mains, high-energy systems, exposed conductors, or unknown equipment, FREEOS should recommend qualified-person procedures rather than direct live-work instructions.

units.title: Electrical reasoning failures
units.content: Avoid measuring resistance on energized circuits, assuming ground is always zero potential, confusing open circuits with shorts, overlooking source current limits, exceeding connector or wire ratings, and treating nominal voltage as proof that a circuit can safely deliver required power.

drills.title: Reason about a low-voltage load
drills.prompt: A 12 V source powers a 24 ohm resistive load. Calculate ideal current and power, then explain what real-world source rating, wire, connector, and heat checks are still needed. Do not propose mains work.

competencies.name: Electronics Fundamentals
competencies.description: Reason about common electronic components, signals, power rails, logic, sensing, and board-level fault isolation.
competencies.purpose: Understand and diagnose low-voltage electronic systems at a functional level.

units.title: Component function before part number
units.content: Understand what a resistor, capacitor, diode, transistor, regulator, sensor, and logic device is doing in the circuit before focusing on its exact part number. Functional role narrows expected signals and likely failure modes.

units.title: Board-level diagnostic sequence
units.content: Start with visual inspection, connector integrity, supply input, protected rails, regulator outputs, reset/enable states, then signal path. Compare against known-good references or datasheets where available. Use current-limited bench methods for safe low-voltage testing when qualified to do so.

units.title: Electronics diagnostic traps
units.content: Avoid probing without a reference ground, injecting power into unknown nodes, replacing ICs before checking rails and enables, interpreting one static voltage as proof of signal integrity, and ignoring thermal or connector-related faults.

drills.title: Diagnose a dead low-voltage controller
drills.prompt: A 5 V controller does not boot. Design a low-voltage diagnostic sequence covering input power, protection, regulator rails, reset/enable, clock or activity indicators, and when to stop for deeper board expertise.

competencies.name: Mechanical Fundamentals
competencies.description: Understand force, torque, friction, load paths, stiffness, motion, bearings, fasteners, and common mechanical failure modes.
competencies.purpose: Reason about mechanical systems and diagnose low-risk faults without unsafe machinery intervention.

units.title: Load paths and constraints
units.content: For any mechanical assembly, trace where forces enter, how they travel through members and joints, where motion is constrained, and where stress concentrates. Geometry and boundary conditions matter as much as nominal material strength.

units.title: Mechanical fault inspection
units.content: De-energize and secure moving equipment before hands-on inspection. Check looseness, wear, alignment, lubrication, interference, abnormal heat, vibration, fastener condition, and bearing play. Compare with expected motion before disassembly.

units.title: Mechanical reasoning failures
units.content: Avoid tightening as a universal fix, using torque values without the correct fastener/material context, ignoring misalignment, operating guards removed, diagnosing rotating equipment by touch while energized, and replacing bearings without correcting the root load or lubrication issue.

drills.title: Analyze a vibrating drive
drills.prompt: A belt-driven machine develops new vibration. Create a safe inspection plan for alignment, belt condition/tension, pulleys, bearings, mounts, and load before replacing parts.

competencies.name: Computer Networking
competencies.description: Understand layered communication, addressing, routing, switching, DNS, ports, latency, and systematic network diagnosis.
competencies.purpose: Design and troubleshoot reliable local and service networks.

units.title: Layered network reasoning
units.content: Separate physical/link connectivity, IP addressing, routing, name resolution, transport ports, TLS, and application behavior. A working ping does not prove DNS, port access, authentication, or application health.

units.title: Network troubleshooting ladder
units.content: Confirm interface/link; inspect address, subnet, gateway, and route; test local gateway; test a known IP; test DNS resolution; test target host and port; inspect TLS/application response; then inspect firewalls, proxies, or service logs. Record where expected behavior first diverges.

units.title: Networking traps
units.content: Avoid changing DNS to fix a physical-link problem, disabling firewalls as a first step, assuming localhost and LAN binding are equivalent, ignoring IPv4 versus IPv6 path differences, and treating timeout, refusal, and name-resolution errors as the same failure.

drills.title: Diagnose an unreachable local service
drills.prompt: A web service works on localhost but not from another device on the LAN. Build a troubleshooting sequence covering bind address, host firewall, route/subnet, port listening, and client testing.

competencies.name: Automation & Control Systems
competencies.description: Understand sensors, actuators, state, feedback, interlocks, sequencing, and failure-safe control design.
competencies.purpose: Design bounded automation that behaves predictably under normal and abnormal conditions.

units.title: Open-loop versus closed-loop control
units.content: Open-loop control commands an action without measuring the result. Closed-loop control measures output and adjusts based on error. Feedback improves regulation but can introduce oscillation, delay sensitivity, noise amplification, or instability if poorly designed.

units.title: Safe sequence design
units.content: Define states, allowed transitions, preconditions, sensor validation, actuator commands, timeouts, fault states, manual override, and recovery. Put interlocks and emergency behavior outside ordinary happy-path logic. Simulate or test at low consequence before connecting hazardous motion or energy.

units.title: Automation design failures
units.content: Avoid assuming sensors cannot fail, allowing commands without state confirmation, using time delays where feedback is required, creating unrecoverable intermediate states, and letting software-only logic substitute for required physical safety interlocks.

drills.title: Design a bounded tank-control sequence
drills.prompt: Design a conceptual fill-and-drain controller using level sensors, valves, timeout faults, sensor disagreement handling, and a safe stopped state. Keep it conceptual rather than wiring real equipment.

competencies.name: Reliability Engineering
competencies.description: Improve uptime and repeatability through failure analysis, preventive actions, observability, redundancy, and verification.
competencies.purpose: Reduce recurring failures and design systems that degrade predictably instead of chaotically.

units.title: Failure mode versus root cause
units.content: A failure mode describes how a system fails; a root cause explains why the conditions for that failure existed. Fixing the visible failed component without addressing the causal mechanism often creates recurrence.

units.title: Reliability improvement loop
units.content: Capture failure context; classify failure mode; preserve evidence; identify contributing conditions; test likely causes; implement containment; implement corrective action; verify under realistic load; monitor recurrence; then update maintenance or design controls.

units.title: Design for detection before failure
units.content: Useful observability, thresholds, logs, wear indicators, and health checks turn surprise failures into planned interventions. Detection quality is part of reliability design.

drills.title: Break a repeat-failure cycle
drills.prompt: A subsystem has failed three times in six months and the same part keeps being replaced. Design an investigation and corrective-action plan that separates failed part, failure mode, contributing conditions, and root cause.

competencies.name: CAD & 3D Technical Modeling
competencies.description: Create dimensionally controlled models that communicate design intent, interfaces, clearances, and manufacturable geometry.
competencies.purpose: Use 3D models as engineering communication and verification artifacts, not only visual representations.

units.title: Parametric modeling workflow
units.content: Establish units and origin; define primary datums; sketch with constraints; dimension design intent rather than accidental geometry; build features in stable dependency order; model interfaces and clearances; then inspect mass, interference, and critical dimensions.

units.title: Constrain intent, not every coordinate
units.content: Good CAD constraints express relationships that should remain true when dimensions change. Over-constraining to current geometry makes future changes fragile.

units.title: CAD failures
units.content: Avoid arbitrary origins, unconstrained sketches, circular dependencies, modeling cosmetic detail before interfaces, zero-clearance assemblies, and exporting meshes without confirming units, scale, normals, or tolerance needs.

drills.title: Plan a mounting bracket model
drills.prompt: Describe how you would model a bracket that must align two bolt patterns and clear a moving component. Define datums, constraints, critical dimensions, clearances, and verification checks.

competencies.name: Manufacturing Fundamentals
competencies.description: Understand process selection, tolerance, material behavior, workholding, inspection, and design-for-manufacture tradeoffs.
competencies.purpose: Design parts and processes that can be made, measured, and repeated safely.

units.title: Process capability drives design detail
units.content: Machining, additive manufacturing, sheet fabrication, molding, casting, and hand fabrication have different achievable tolerances, surface finish, geometry limits, setup costs, and economics. Match tolerances and features to the process actually being used.

units.title: Manufacturing planning checklist
units.content: Define function, material, quantity, critical dimensions, tolerance, surface needs, available processes, workholding or support strategy, inspection method, and safety controls. Prototype high-uncertainty interfaces before committing to expensive production.

units.title: Manufacturing planning failures
units.content: Avoid specifying tight tolerances everywhere, ignoring tool access or print orientation, creating uninspectable critical dimensions, assuming nominal CAD equals finished part, bypassing guards/PPE, and using unfamiliar powered machinery without qualified supervision.

drills.title: Choose a manufacturing process
drills.prompt: Compare CNC machining, FDM printing, and sheet fabrication for a low-volume bracket. Discuss geometry, tolerance, finish, strength direction, lead time, cost, and inspection.
